'''class SpaStaticFiles(StaticFiles):
    """Static files with a single-page-app fallback.

    ``html=True`` alone only serves index.html for directory paths, so a client
    -side route like /datasets/abc/explore 404s -- in-app navigation works but a
    refresh or a shared link does not. Unknown paths therefore fall back to
    index.html and let the router resolve them.

    Two kinds of path are excluded, both because answering them with HTML turns
    a missing thing into a baffling one:

    * ``/api/`` -- a typo'd endpoint would reach the caller as a JSON parse
      error rather than a 404.
    * anything that names a file -- a missing asset would be served as an HTML
      page with a 200, and whatever tried to load it fails somewhere far away.
      This is not hypothetical: a missing worker chunk was served as index.html,
      the module worker died parsing HTML as JavaScript, and the only visible
      symptom was a map that drew no points.

    A client-side route has no file extension, which is what separates the two.
    """

    async def get_response(self, path: str, scope):
        try:
            return await super().get_response(path, scope)
        except StarletteHTTPException as exc:
            if exc.status_code != 404:
                raise
            if path.startswith("api/") or "." in path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]:
                raise
            return await super().get_response("index.html", scope)''')
p.write_text(s)

'''// maplibre resolves its worker at runtime as
// `new URL('./maplibre-gl-worker.mjs', import.meta.url)` with a computed

class SpaStaticFiles(StaticFiles):
    """Static files with a single-page-app fallback.

    ``html=True`` alone only serves index.html for directory paths, so a client
    -side route like /datasets/abc/explore 404s -- in-app navigation works but a
    refresh or a shared link does not. Unknown paths therefore fall back to
    index.html and let the router resolve them.

    Unknown ``/api/`` paths keep their 404: answering them with an HTML page
    would turn a typo'd endpoint into a confusing parse error at the caller.
    """

    async def get_response(self, path: str, scope):
        try:
            return await super().get_response(path, scope)
        except StarletteHTTPException as exc:
            if exc.status_code != 404 or path.startswith("api/"):
                raise
            return await super().get_response("index.html", scope)

This is the root cause of the current bug — it masks missing /assets/* files as 200 HTML.

frontend/src/renderers/MapLibreRenderer.tsx — current header:

// maplibre-gl v6 is named-exports-only; it dropped the default export that
// react-map-gl 8.x still expects.
import {
  Map as MapLibreMap,
  setWorkerUrl,
  type GeoJSONSource,
  type StyleSpecification,
} from 'maplibre-gl'
// maplibre resolves its worker at runtime as
// `new URL('./maplibre-gl-worker.mjs', import.meta.url)` with a computed
// filename, which no bundler can see -- so the asset is never emitted and the
// worker 404s. Importing it with ?url makes Vite emit and fingerprint it, then
// setWorkerUrl points maplibre at the real thing. Without this, GeoJSON layers
// draw nothing while the raster basemap (which needs no worker) looks fine.
import maplibreWorkerUrl from 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs?url'

setWorkerUrl(maplibreWorkerUrl)

def test_unknown_dataset_is_404(client):
    assert client.get("/api/datasets/nope").status_code == 404
    assert client.get("/api/datasets/nope/profile").status_code == 404
    assert client.get("/api/plugins?applicable_to=nope").status_code == 404


def test_spa_deep_links_fall_back_to_index(app_ctx, tmp_path):
    """A client-side route must survive a refresh or a shared link.

    StaticFiles(html=True) only serves index.html for *directory* paths, so
    without a fallback /datasets/abc/explore 404s: in-app navigation works but
    reloading the page does not.
    """
    from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

    import dataq.api.app as app_module

    dist = tmp_path / "dist"
    dist.mkdir()
    (dist / "index.html").write_text("<!doctype html><title>DataQ</title>")
    (dist / "assets").mkdir()
    (dist / "assets" / "app.js").write_text("console.log(1)")

    app_ctx.settings.static_dir = dist
    app = create_app(ctx=app_ctx)
    try:
        with TestClient(app) as client:
            assert client.get("/").status_code == 200
            # Client-side routes resolve to the shell.
            for route in ("/datasets", "/datasets/abc123/explore", "/dashboards", "/ask"):
                r = client.get(route)
                assert r.status_code == 200, route
                assert "DataQ" in r.text, route
            # Real assets are still served as themselves.
            assert client.get("/assets/app.js").text == "console.log(1)"
            # An unknown API path stays a 404 rather than becoming an HTML page,
            # which would surface at the caller as a JSON parse error.
            missing = client.get("/api/does-not-exist")
            assert missing.status_code == 404
            assert "<!doctype html>" not in missing.text.lower()
    finally:
        app_module.CTX = None

$ Bash
Verify points actually render in a browser
cat > "$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/verify-map.mjs" <<'EOF'
import { chromium } from 'playwright-core'

const URL = 'http://localhost:8000/datasets/1b59c830bbf1/explore'
const browser = await chromium.launch({
  channel: 'chrome', headless: true,
})
const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1400, height: 950 } })

const failed = [], errors = []
page.on('requestfailed', r => failed.push(`${r.url()} ${r.failure()?.errorText}`))
page.on('console', m => { if (m.type() === 'error') errors.push(m.text()) })
page.on('response', async r => {
  // The exact failure mode we are hunting: a JS asset served as HTML.
  if (/\.(m?js)(\?|$)/.test(r.url()) && (r.headers()['content-type'] || '').includes('text/html'))
    errors.push(`ASSET SERVED AS HTML: ${r.url()}`)
})

await page.goto(URL, { waitUntil: 'networkidle', timeout: 60000 })

// Find and click the map suggestion.
const mapBtn = page.getByText(/Map of (pickup locations|points)/i).first()
if (await mapBtn.count()) { await mapBtn.click(); await page.waitForTimeout(1000) }

// Wait for maplibre to finish loading tiles + data.
await page.waitForFunction(() => document.querySelectorAll('.maplibregl-canvas').length > 0,
  null, { timeout: 30000 }).catch(() => {})
await page.waitForTimeout(9000)

const result = await page.evaluate(() => {
  const canvases = [...document.querySelectorAll('.maplibregl-canvas')]
  const out = { canvases: canvases.length, painted: [] }
  for (const c of canvases) {
    // Read the pixels back: the only honest test of "does it draw points".
    const gl = c.getContext('webgl2', { preserveDrawingBuffer: true })
      || c.getContext('webgl', { preserveDrawingBuffer: true })
    if (!gl) { out.painted.push('no-gl'); continue }
    const w = gl.drawingBufferWidth, h = gl.drawingBufferHeight
    const px = new Uint8Array(w * h * 4)
    gl.readPixels(0, 0, w, h, gl.RGBA, gl.UNSIGNED_BYTE, px)
    // Points are drawn in a saturated blue; the basemap is grey/tan.
    let blue = 0
    for (let i = 0; i < px.length; i += 4) {
      const [r, g, b, a] = [px[i], px[i+1], px[i+2], px[i+3]]
      if (a > 40 && b > 110 && b - r > 45 && b - g > 25) blue++
    }
    out.painted.push({ w, h, bluePixels: blue })
  }
  out.readout = document.body.innerText.match(/[\d,]+ points/)?.[0] ?? null
  return out
})

console.log(JSON.stringify({ result, failed, errors }, null, 2))
await page.screenshot({ path: process.env.CLAUDE_JOB_DIR + '/tmp/map-after.png' })
await browser.close()
EOF
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"; cd frontend && node "$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/verify-map.mjs" 2>&1 | tail -40

Fix the map in the production bundle, and stop hiding missing assets

Two bugs, one hiding the other.

The map drew no points in the container while working fine under the Vite
dev server. maplibre's worker chunk imports a sibling, maplibre-gl-shared.mjs.
The `?url` import copied the worker file verbatim as an asset without
following that import, so the sibling was never emitted. `?worker&url` bundles
the worker with its dependency graph instead -- one self-contained 476 kB
chunk, and the dev server resolves it the same way.

The reason this took so long to find is the second bug. The SPA fallback
answered *any* unmatched path with index.html and a 200, so the missing chunk
came back as an HTML page. The module worker died parsing HTML as JavaScript,
silently, inside the worker: no console error, no failed request, just a
basemap with nothing on it. The fallback's own docstring already argued the
right principle for /api/ -- an HTML answer turns a missing thing into a
confusing one somewhere far away -- and that reasoning applies just as well to
files. A client-side route has no file extension, which is what separates the
two cases.

The test now asserts a missing asset 404s. On the first run after the fix a
real 404 surfaced immediately, which is the point: it was /favicon.ico, the
browser's automatic probe, previously masked as a 200 HTML page.

Verified in a headless browser against yellow_tripdata_2016-02 in the
container: 20,000 pickup points over Manhattan on both the static and animated
maps. (The obvious check -- reading pixels back off the canvas -- is a false
negative here; maplibre's GL context has no preserveDrawingBuffer, so the
buffer is cleared after compositing and readPixels returns all zeros whether
or not anything drew.)

Assistant2026-08-29T00:18:40.406Z

No — it was not a Vite server issue. The container serves a prebuilt bundle from /app/static; no Vite is involved at all. Two separate bugs, one hiding the other:

1. The actual break. maplibre's worker chunk imports a sibling, maplibre-gl-shared.mjs. My ?url import copied the worker file verbatim as an asset without following that import, so the sibling was never emitted by the build. Switching to ?worker&url bundles the worker with its dependency graph — one self-contained 476 kB chunk. The dev server worked only because it resolves imports on the fly.

2. Why it was so hard to see. My SPA fallback answered any unmatched path with index.html and a 200. So the missing chunk came back as an HTML page, and the module worker died parsing HTML as JavaScript — silently, inside the worker. No console error, no failed request, just a basemap with nothing on it. The fallback's own docstring already made the right argument for /api/ paths; it just didn't apply it to files. A client-side route has no file extension, which is what separates the two cases.

Verified in the container at :8000 against yellow_tripdata_2016-02 — 20,000 pickup points over Manhattan on both the static and animated maps.

Worth flagging: my first verification attempt read pixels back off the canvas and reported zero blue pixels, which looked like the fix had failed. That test was invalid — maplibre's GL context has no preserveDrawingBuffer, so the buffer is cleared after compositing and readPixels returns zeros regardless. The screenshot is what actually confirmed it.

One incidental find: with the masking gone, a real 404 surfaced on the very first load — /favicon.ico, the browser's automatic probe. Harmless, and the app's declared /favicon.svg serves fine, but it had been invisible.

  • Committed as 3853b41 on main (324 backend tests pass, typecheck clean).
  • The container is running the rebuilt dataq:latest on port 8000 — I replaced the manually-started nice_ramanujan container with an identical docker run (same /data mount and env), since it held the port.
